data.narrative:
Stratek Global is a growth-stage nuclear energy company founded by Kelvin Kemm. The valuation exercise draws from a comp universe of 8 peers: 3 public companies (OKLO, NNE, SMR) and 5 private firms (Oklo, X-Energy, Nano Nuclear Energy, Fuse Energy, Blue Energy), all operating in the nuclear energy sector.

The peer-median triangulation method is not applicable here. The nuclear energy sector contains only 4 same-sector peers overall, but none satisfy the filtering criteria for stage alignment or valuation-tier clustering required to yield a sufficiently robust dataset (minimum 3 datapoints). Applying a broad sector median would introduce material measurement error given the structural heterogeneity within nuclear energy financing and development timelines. This constraint eliminates the primary quantitative anchor for valuation.

Without a sufficiently dense peer cohort meeting stage and tier criteria, this analysis cannot produce a defensible point estimate or range. Further work requires either: (1) acquisition of additional comparable transaction data within nuclear energy at the growth stage, (2) expansion to adjacent frontier-energy sectors with comparable technical and capital intensity profiles, or (3) engagement with revenue or cash-flow-based methods if Stratek Global's financial profile is available. The core uncertainty is the absence of comparable transactions—a limitation of the frontier-energy financing landscape rather than a deficiency in methodology.
